name: long pause mid-sentence
why: A 2.5 s word gap (about 2.3 s of real silence) while looking for a word is the main thing the player should point at.
script: I went to the [2.5 pause] store today

name: word gap of 1.6 s
why: Grok word gaps read about 0.2 s long. 1.6 s is a real 1.4 s breath and must not be flagged.
script: I went to the [1.6 not pause] store today

name: word gap of exactly 1.7 s
why: 1.7 s between Grok words is a real 1.5 s silence. Rounding in word times must not drop it.
script: I went to the [1.7 pause] store today

name: silence before the first word
why: Freezing at the start is a pause too.
script: [2.0 pause] So I think we should go

name: short silence before the first word
why: A normal breath before starting is not a freeze.
script: [1.0 not pause] So I think we should go

name: silence after the last word
why: Stopping early is not a pause inside the talk.
script: I think that is all [5.0 not pause]

name: two fillers within 6 s
why: A cluster of fillers marks a moment of searching.
script: I <fillers> um think it was really nice and then I went uh </> home

name: two fillers more than 6 s apart
why: Fillers spread across a talk are normal speech, not one stuck moment.
script: So <not fillers> um we drove to the coast on a sunny day and the water was calm so we stayed by the beach for a long time until uh </> lunch

name: one filler
why: A single um is not worth a marker.
script: I <not fillers> um </> think so

name: three fillers close together
why: The note should count all three.
script: So <fillers> um I uh think er </> yes

name: fillers with punctuation and capitals
why: Grok writes “Um,” at sentence starts. It is still a filler.
script: <fillers> Um, I went uh, </> home

name: restart of one word
why: “I I went” is a restart.
script: <restart> I I </> went home

name: restart of three words
why: “I went to, I went to the store” is a restart.
script: <restart> I went to I went to </> the store

name: restart of a short function word
why: “to to the store” is a stumble, not emphasis.
script: I went <restart> to to </> the store

name: restart with a filler between
why: “I, um, I went” is still a restart, and one filler is not a cluster.
script: <restart> I um I </> went home

name: repeat after a long pause
why: If 2 s pass between the copies it is a pause, not a quick restart.
script: <not restart> I went [2.0 pause] I went </> home

name: emphasis repeat
why: “very very good” is emphasis, not a restart.
script: It was <not restart> very very </> good

name: grammatical repeat
why: “I think that that is true” is correct English.
script: I think <not restart> that that </> is true

name: emphasis no no
why: “No no, that is fine” is emphasis.
script: <not restart> No no </> that is fine

name: cap keeps the three longest pauses on a 1-minute take
why: A 1-minute take shows at most 3 markers. The longest hesitations win.
script: one [9 pause] two [8 pause] three [2 pause maybe] four [7 pause] five [1.8 pause maybe] six

name: two close pauses keep the longer
why: Markers must sit at least 13% of the take apart, so the scrubber stays tappable.
script: I went [4 pause] to the shop [3 pause maybe] for milk

name: take under 30 s still gets markers
why: Short takes do not count toward the report, but they still get feedback.
script: So I [2.0 pause] think it went well

name: very short take shows one marker, the biggest
why: A 6 s take gets one marker. A 2.3 s filler cluster beats a 1.8 s word gap.
script: I [1.8 pause maybe] <fillers> um went to uh the er </> store

name: pause inside a filler cluster
why: One stuck moment should get one marker, not two on top of each other.
script: So <fillers> um [2.0 pause maybe] uh </> I think

name: clean take
why: Fluent speech gets no markers.
script: I like to walk to work because it is quiet and I can think about the day

name: reading: clean read
why: Reading the passage as written gets no markers.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: skipped content word
why: Skipping “old” changes the picture. It should be shown.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed past the [0.1 skip] lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: several skipped words become one marker
why: “past the old” dropped together is one moment, not three.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed [0.1 skip] lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: dropped function word is ignored
why: Grok often drops “the”. Flagging it would be noise.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed past [0.1 not skip] old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: minimal-pair swap
why: “sheep” for “ship” is the contrast the passage trains.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The <swap> sheep </> sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: near-miss ending is not a swap
why: “sail” for “sailed” is a clipped ending, which ASR does often. Not worth a marker.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship <not swap> sail </> past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: self-correction is not flagged
why: Rereading “the old” to fix it is good reading, not an error.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed past the old the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: fillers are ignored
why: Reading markers are about the words, not fillers.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed past <not fillers> um the old uh </> lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: pauses are not markers
why: Reading markers are about the words, not pauses.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed [3.0 not pause] past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.

name: reading: stopping early is not a skip
why: The unread rest of the passage is already in the report. It is not a listen-back moment.
passage: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse at dawn while the river ran fast.
script: The ship sailed past the old lighthouse

name: conversation: slow start
why: Taking 3 s to start answering is the freeze Conversation trains against.
script: {2.0 What do you do on weekends?} [3.0 slowstart] Usually I go hiking with friends
noteContains: After “What do you do on weekends?”, you took 3 seconds

name: conversation: quick answer
why: Answering within a second is normal timing, even for L2 speakers.
script: {2.0 What do you do on weekends?} [1.0 not slowstart] Usually I go hiking with friends

name: conversation: wait just under the line
why: About 1.9 s is inside a beginner's normal range. Not flagged.
script: {2.0 What do you do?} [2.0 not slowstart] I work at a bakery

name: conversation: wait just over the line
why: About 2.1 s is past a beginner's normal range.
script: {2.0 What do you do?} [2.2 slowstart] I work at a bakery

name: conversation: the partner's turn is not a pause
why: Silence on the mic while the partner talks is not the user pausing.
script: I like hiking {3.0 Where do you go?} [0.5 not slowstart] Mostly the hills near home

name: conversation: pause inside an answer
why: A long freeze mid-answer is flagged, the same as in Monologue.
script: {2.0 What do you do?} [0.6] I work at a [2.5 pause] bakery near home

name: conversation: fillers inside an answer
why: A filler cluster mid-answer is flagged.
script: {2.0 Why that job?} [0.5] I <fillers> um think it was uh </> the hours

name: conversation: fillers split by the partner are not a cluster
why: One um before the partner speaks and one after are two separate answers.
script: I think <not fillers> um {2.0 Really?} [0.5] uh </> yes

name: conversation: no answer before the partner speaks again
why: If the partner talks again before the user answers, there is no answer to time.
script: {2.0 Hi there.} [4.0 not slowstart] {2.0 Are you still there?} [0.5] Yes sorry
